steps.text: Preheat oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).
Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil. Add pasta and cook for 8 to 10 minutes or until al dente; drain.

In a large saucepan over medium heat, melt 2 tablespoons butter. Whisk in flour and cook, stirring, 1 minute. A little at a time, whisk in milk, mustard, salt, pepper and hot sauce. Bring to a gentle boil, stirring constantly. Boil 1 minute, then remove from heat and whisk in pepperjack, Cheddar and Parmesan until smooth. Stir in cooked pasta and pour into shallow 2 quart baking dish.
Melt remaining 2 tablespoons butter. Stir in bread crumbs and chili powder. Sprinkle over macaroni mixture.
Bake in preheated oven 30 minutes. Let stand 10 minutes before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Kicked Up Mac and Cheese
raw_recipe.description: Macaroni and cheese spiked with hot pepper sauce, dry mustard, jalapeno cheese and chili powder.

video.description: This cheesy, spicy, creamy mac and cheese is way better than the boxed stuff! With three kinds of cheese - pepperjack, Cheddar and Parmesan - and a kick of heat from hot sauce and chili powder, this may be your new go-to mac and cheese recipe!

review.reviewBody: This recipe is awesome!! We all loved it, even my one-year old. (I did cut back on the hot pepper sauce). I put the chili powder (and a little less) into the sauce and used a mix of 2% and 1% milk. I used more pasta too, probably 2.5 cups and I could have used more, but I like an extra cheesey, saucey sauce opposed to a drier sauce. We had broccoli with this and spooned some of the extra sauce over that. I used radiatore pasta in this and it was wonderful. Shredded my own parm, used Tillamook Pepperjack and Tillamook Extra Sharp Reserve White Cheddar cheese. Used a bit extra of all the cheeses. LOVED it!!! I used crushed garlic croutons in place of bread crumbs and butter. We couldn't get enough. I will make this again.

My family loves spicy foods. This is a favorite! I make it without the topping. It’s a great winter dinner. I often make chili and use this on top as a southwestern shepherd’s pie. I often don’t use the pepperjack cheese and just double the cheddar. When I used packaged grated cheese, the texture was off, a bit gritty. It’s turns out the additives used to prevent clumping in the package, prevents the cheese from having the correct texture. Grating my own cheese gave the correct creamy texture.

I made some variations based on what I had available. Here is my version:

Ingredients:
2 cups elbow pasta
4 tablespoons butter, divided
1/4 cup all-purpose flour
3 cups skim milk (fresh from local farm)
1 teaspoon dry mustard
1/2 teaspoon salt 
1/2 teaspoon ground white pepper
1/4 - 1/2 teaspoons ground cayenne pepper
1/4 cup shredded mild blue cheese
1 1/2 cups shredded white LIVAROT or something very similar to this. (ripped off the label and can't remember the name, but it is considered a stinky cheese and has a mild flavor. Or Havarti will work, but you'll have to cut it up because it's too soft to shred.)
1/2 cup grated 5 yr aged GRUYERE
1 medium clove chopped shallot
1/3 cup chopped onion
1-3 cloves garlic
1 teaspoons ground cayenne pepper

Directions:
Preheat oven to 375 degrees F.
Cook pasta until al dente; drain.
In a small saucepan melt 2 tablespoons butter, add in shallots, onions and garlic simmer until caramelized. Once caramelized stir in 1 tsp cayenne powder. 
In a large saucepan over medium heat, melt 2 tablespoons butter. Whisk in flour and cook, stirring, 1 minute. A little at a time, whisk in milk, mustard, salt, pepper and hot sauce. Bring to a gentle boil, stirring constantly. Boil 1 minute, then remove from heat and whisk in shredded cheeses until smooth. Stir in cooked pasta and pour into shallow 2 quart baking dish.
Sprinkle shallot mixture over macaroni mixture.
Bake in preheated oven 30 minutes. Let stand 10 minutes before serving.

The first time I made this my roux looked like a ball of dough, rather than a smooth buttery paste. That's when I noticed the roux proportions were off: roux should be 1 part flour to 1 part butter. 1/4 cup of flour = 4 tbsp flour, so you should be using 4 tbsp butter. The ingredients do list 4 tbsp butter, but then the directions encourage, "melt 2 tablespoons butter, whisk in flour" and reserve the remaining two tbsp butter for the topping later on. Wrong!

So! My second go, I used 4 tbsp flour, 4 tbsp butter, on medium low to get the nice smooth paste. I substituted shredded Gruyere for the sharp cheddar (didn't have any on hand) and skipped the butter/breadcrumb/chili powder topping altogether. I also skipped the baking because I wanted a creamy, hot, stovetop version.

Thought the sauce ended up a bit bland (I like hot) and runny, so I mixed in about 1 tbsp of the chili powder I ignored earlier and a little Worcestershire, plus a bit more Sriracha. Let it sit over medium heat without stirring to thicken it up for a few minutes, then I dumped the creamy sauce all over my pot of cooked elbows and stirred.

OH GOD, now that was good. Minus a star for the roux.

IMy family really enjoyed this dish! Changes: added 1 pkg frozen baby broccoli florets, reduced hot sauce to 1 tsp, added @ 1 tsp nutmeg to sauce mixture, added 1-2 tsp garlic powder (powder, not salt), omitted extra salt, used herb-seasoned stuffing mix for topping (instead of bread crumbs). Everyone had seconds -- and that's a first!

This recipe rocks. It has flavor. Lots of flavor. I nix cheap cheese and used a good quality cheddar and some mid-quality jack without the peppers. Don't make the mistake of using elbow macs. It doesn't work. I used everything else exactly. But - You can leave off the bread crumb topping and it browns nicely without it.

To the person who is confused about the flour and butter - Yes, it's supposed to ball up. You are making a basic white sauce. Stir it constantly as you pour in the milk in small amounts. It will thicken the milk while breaking up those small balls of butter and flour.

I made this recipe for the first time today when some family came over for dinner. I used just under 8 cups of pasta and added more cheese which was great for serving seven adults. It's important to make sure you have the sauce pan at medium heat and maybe even on the higher side when starting to mix the butter and flour so that the following ingredients will thicken properly to create the cheese mixture. If you want to add some extra kick to the bread crumbs try adding 1/4 teaspoon of cayenne pepper before sprinkling them over the dish prior to baking. Also, I like my mac and cheese a little more well done so I let it cook for around 40 minutes and it came out golden brown. Overall, it was an enjoyable dish that didn't take much effort and the family loved it!

This was a big hit with both of my gourmet teenage boys. We used Italian bread crumbs, Parmesan, chili pwdr & paprika for the crust (no melting) just sprinkled it all on there. It made a tasty, crunchy top. 
I added horseradish to the mix. And, I sautéed an onion and clove of garlic (minced) before adding thickener.

This was great! I didn't add breadcrumbs nor bake it. Instead I cooked the pasta thoroughly, then made the sauce and poured it on top. I ended up with way too much cheese sauce for the amount of pasta I made, but I was using gluten free fusilli pasta so maybe the measurement for that was off.

I made this for thanksgiving and everyone loved it. Only baked for 10 minutes not wanting it to dry out. I used shell pasta and added a can of diced green chiles, other than that made exactly as stated. Yummy! Will definitely make again!
Everyone loved it, I accidentally forgot the Parmesan so just threw it on at then end as part of the crust with the breadcrumbs.
Great flavor. More bread crumbs make a better topping
Great!
I've been waiting for this recipe my whole life and didn't know it! I've made it twice this week. I've never been able to make Mac and Cheese to my liking until now. Thank you for this recipe!
Made it twice so far; big hit with our grandchildren (late teens/early 20s)
Even tho cut back on hot sauce we both found it too hot for our tastes!
This really is a great recipe! Whole family loves it. I don’t change anything.
I didn't care for it. I think it was the topping that ruined it for me...it was dry. I loved the pepper jack though.

This is now my go-to mac and cheese recipe. I use Valentina hot sauce, which is the best hot sauce out there IMO. I added one tsp of chili powder to the cheese mix and only used one tsp for the breadcrumbs. I also finely chop some onion (about half a cup) and toss it in the cheese mix for a little bit of crunch and flavour.
Yum
